post.description:
Initiate OAuth authorization flow for a provider.

Steps:
1. Validate provider is supported
2. Generate OAuth state and PKCE parameters
3. Create PENDING connection in PostgreSQL
4. Store state in memcached for callback validation
5. Return OAuth authorization URL

Args:
    provider: Provider name (google, microsoft, etc.)
    request: Authorization request with user_id

Returns:
    JSON with auth_url to redirect user to

get.description:
Handle OAuth callback from provider.

Steps:
1. Validate state parameter
2. Handle any OAuth errors
3. Exchange authorization code for tokens
4. Store encrypted credentials in PostgreSQL
5. Update connection status to CONNECTED
6. Redirect to success page

Args:
    provider: Provider name
    code: Authorization code from provider
    state: State parameter for validation
    error: Optional error from provider
    error_description: Optional error description

Returns:
    HTML success page or redirect

List all available MCP servers for a user, including both connected and unconnected.

This endpoint returns all MCP apps that are available through OAuth providers

connected and enabled. This allows the frontend to display "Connect" buttons
for unconnected services.

Retrieve a specific MCP service for a user.

This endpoint returns details for a single MCP service formatted the same way
as items in the list_provider_servers list. Useful for checking the status
of a specific service after enabling/disabling or for focused UI updates.

Args:
    provider: Provider name (google, microsoft, etc.)
    service: Service/app identifier (e.g., "drive", "google_drive", "sheets", etc.)
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    Single server object with provider, app_id, connected status, enabled status, etc.

post.description:

delete.description:
Delete one explicit phrase when a body is supplied, otherwise wipe all.

The legacy query-only shape ``DELETE /user_memory?user_id=...`` still
removes every stored record. A JSON body with ``phrase`` or ``key`` uses the
new explicit forget matcher instead.

get.description:
List saved memory records by bucket for UI management.

Bucket names match the delete route's ``kind`` path parameter, so the UI
can pass an item's bucket name and key directly to ``DELETE /user_memory/{kind}/{key}``.
When ``conversationId`` is provided, the payload is emitted to the Socket.IO
room named by that conversation and the HTTP response is only an acknowledgement.

patch.description:
Merge ``patch`` into the existing profile record.

Creates the profile if none exists. Fields set to ``None`` on the patch
leave the existing value untouched; callers must send an explicit empty
list to clear a list field. Shares the per-user write lock with the
explicit API and ambient extractor so the single profile row is never
clobbered by a concurrent writer.

patch.description:
Update a collection memory record's strength by bucket and key.

Strength is only meaningful on collection buckets. Profile has no strength,
so callers should use ``PATCH /user_memory/profile`` for profile updates.
